text: On the MultiRC testbed, we evaluated a weak-to-strong generalization method that averages labels from an ensemble of weak supervisors, running 10 seeds. The measured performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.2, with a standard error of 0.11. No baseline PGR was supplied in the data provided, so this number cannot be positioned as an improvement over, or a regression from, any alternative approach; it should be read only as a standalone estimate of how much of the weak-to-strong gap this method recovers. The standard error is large relative to the point estimate, spanning a range wide enough that the underlying value could plausibly be considerably lower or higher than 0.2, and with 10 seeds the precision remains limited. Readers should therefore treat the 0.2 figure as provisional. Establishing whether ensemble label averaging helps would require a matched baseline run and additional seeds to tighten the interval around the estimate.
